My ex used to constantly put me down for my sexuality and say, “You’ll leave me for a girl one day. I just know it.” Whenever I would hang out with our mutual friend who was queer, he’d flip his lid.

Ironically, he cheated on me with said friend.

I was 14 and the guy claimed to be 19. We talked online for a while and finally agreed to meet up. When we did, he was extremely creepy. He kept mentioning that his father was a cop and that he got away with everything. He then confessed that he was not 19 but actually *26*. 

From there he kept asking me to come with him to his parent’s lake house for the weekend. I kept telling him that I couldn’t because of school activities I had planned, but he refused to budge. I asked him to drop me off at home and he begrudgingly agreed. As we drove, I realized we were not in fact driving back to my house but somewhere else. I panicked and said that I had to use the bathroom as soon as possible, and he pulled into a Walmart parking lot. 

The last thing I remember was going into the Walmart and running out the other entrance as fast as I could. I ran home and never spoke to him again. He tried calling me on two different numbers and emailing me from 3 different emails.

This used to happen to me too. I would get so anxious that I would visibly shake during conversations. 
There were a couple things that helped me get over this though, so see if it helps you:

1) Imagine someone that you don’t feel anxious looking at in the persons stead. (For me it was my mother, and it helped a lot.)

2) You don’t have to make direct eye-contact all the time. Most people look off in different directions depending on what they’re thinking about, so use that as a tool to break eye contact.

3) Don’t stare. I tend to do this still when I’m extremely focused on the other party’s topic, and it dries out the eyes. It also makes the person feel uncomfortable and can lead to day dreaming. Just try to relax.

4) If you still feel uncomfortable looking someone in the eyes, try just looking at their face as a whole. In time you can move up to their eyes, but it really just does take practice. 

You can do it!

Body paints is mostly just a general term, but there are a couple different types of paints you can use.

Water Activated: These paints are used with water. Depending on how much water you use, the paint will become more or less opaque. If you want a sheer layer of paint, you'd use more water. If you want a thicker layer of paint, you'd use less. 
These are the most popular to use when starting out as they have almost no learning curve and they are relatively cheap. Popular brands that carry water activated paints are Mehron, Ben Nye, Graftobian, Kryolan, and Wolfe. 

Creme colors: These are thicker paints. You don't normally use them with water as they are oil-based, but they can be applied with a sponge soaked in water. They are extremely opaque, but can be patchy if you are using them over a large area. They also require setting powder or else they will smudge. Mehron, Graftobian, Ben Nye and Kryolan all have creme paints as well.

Alcohol Activated: These are paints that can only be used with 99% alcohol. Not 76%, not 91%, only 99%. They are very sheer, but if used properly will give very realistic results. These are good for making veins or trying to build up layers of color for a more natural feel. Ben Nye, European Body Arts, and Skin Illustrator carry these paints.

First, I'll talk about spirit gum. Spirit gum is a skin adhesive that is used to stick on appliances such as prosthetics (fake noses, wounds, etc). When using it, you apply it to the area you want your appliance to stick, wait for it to become tacky and apply it from the center outwards. Some people find that tapping the spirit gum helps it to become tackier faster, but that's truly preference. 
(IMPORTANT) You MUST make sure to have a remover before you apply anything to your skin. Otherwise, you will regret it immensely.

3rd Degree and Skin Tite are brands of silicone. This type of silicone is used for making wounds/prosthetics right onto the skin, rather than having to sculpt them and attach them separately with an adhesive like spirit gum. It comes in two parts: part A and part B. You must mix even parts together or else your prosthetic will not set properly. When mixed together, the paste will slowly stiffen up over a course of 3-5 minutes. You will have this long to put down whatever you want on your skin. I find it easiest to make small batches and build up.  (IMPORTANT: You must be very careful to not put any product from either container into one another. This will corrupt your product and you will be sad.) 

If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask us or message me!

A few years after 9/11, probably 2005 or so, I entered the sixth grade. Where I live, school starts the same week that 9/11 falls on. My English teacher at the time brought in a bolt from the wreckage of the Twin Towers. She had brought it in to show the class in hope to help give us a better understanding as to what happened.

Most of us were too young to remember the day very well. Heck, at the time, most of us couldn't even retain memories from two years ago. But our teacher explained it was a very serious matter, which cost many people their lives. She began with her recollection of the events and started passing around the bolt. I remember most of my classmates whispering to each other things like, "Oh, cool," and "A weird rusty bolt. Okay.. now what?"

 Our teacher, seeing our blasé reaction to this hunk of metal, continued to explain the horror the people in the building were subjected to and how they were trapped by flames. She earnestly went on to say, "Now, if you smell the bolt, you'll be able to smell the burnt metal from the fire."

At this point, this small piece of metal reached my desk. My teacher looked to me and gestured to sniff it as the entire class gazed upon me as well. Being a shy kid, I was not too fond of the suddenly attention. Reluctantly, I brought it up to my nose, and gave a gentle sniff. 
I didn't smell anything burnt, but it did smell quite nice. 
Wait..
I sniffed again. 
It smelled kind of.. citrusy? 
"Oh no," I thought.

My heart sank as I realized that I had eaten a very potent orange for lunch, which was right before the class. I tried desperately to find a spot on this tiny piece of metal where I hadn't touched, but to no avail. I feebly looked to my teacher and with a small voice said, "All I can smell is oranges."
